Synopsis:
Unusually high jellyfish concentrations are impacting Delaware beaches in summer 2024, driven by warmer waters, drought-elevated salinity, favourable wind/circulation patterns, and a quiet hurricane season. Sting rates of 100–200/day are deterring swimmers. Scientists link conditions to climate change and warn these dynamics may become more frequent. A parallel marine heatwave is driving stingray incidents in Southern California.
